answer.original_source: The Motley Fool report (Robert Izquierdo, Aug 1 2026); the Google Cloud figures attribute to Alphabet's Q2 results, which the article does not cite directly
answer.new_information: Supports only the statement that Google Cloud Q2 2026 revenue was reported at $24.8B, up 82% year over year, with backlog above $500B versus $462B in Q1. Material unknowns: the record gives no exact filing date or primary document, no definition of backlog beyond 'customer orders', and no link between Google Cloud's spending and NVDA revenue. The Nvidia parts of the article ($81.6B April quarter, $91B guidance, Vera Rubin) are restatements of company data with no stored questions to attach to. Resolving evidence would be Alphabet's Q2 2026 10-Q and earnings release, and any NVDA disclosure naming Google as a customer with a dollar amount.
answer.independent_judgement: No investment question is supported by this record. Alphabet is outside the covered scope (NVDA), and the Google Cloud growth and backlog figures do not show NVDA demand. Any NVDA-relevant conclusion would need a bridge such as Alphabet's capex or AI-chip purchase disclosures tying Google Cloud growth to NVDA shipments, and this record provides none.
answer.reason: The record is a third-party media article about Alphabet, not NVDA. It contains no stored pieces or questions to update, and its only NVDA-related content is secondhand restatement of company figures already in the record, so it is background context only. Its Alphabet claims are relayed from company results and do not contest or confirm any existing NVDA argument.
